walkthroughs.body_html:
Automated & Emerging Technologies — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Automated & Emerging Technologies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Automated & Emerging Technologies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An automated system is made up of:
options: Sensors, a microprocessor and actuators
Only a keyboard and a screen
A printer and a scanner
Cables and routers only

mcqs.q: Which is a typical characteristic of a robot?
options: It can be reprogrammed to carry out different physical tasks
It must look like a human
It cannot work for more than an hour
It always thinks like a person
Learning patterns from data and feedback
Being rebuilt with new hardware each time
Following a fixed list of rules that never changes
Asking the user to solve each problem

mcqs.q: One advantage of automating a production task is:
options: Consistent operation around the clock without tiredness
The system designs new products by itself
No electricity is needed
Mistakes become impossible in every situation

mcqs.q: Are AI and robots the same thing?
options: No - AI is software that exhibits intelligent behaviour, while a robot is a physical machine; robots may or may not use AI, and most AI runs without any robot body.
Yes - AI is just the brand name for industrial robots.
Yes - automated systems repair and reprogram themselves completely.
Yes - anything with AI is a robot and every robot has AI.

mcqs.q: Is a machine learning system given explicit rules for every situation?
options: Yes - programmers write a rule for every case the system might meet.
Yes - AI is just the brand name for industrial robots.
No - it is trained on data and learns the patterns itself; that is what distinguishes it from traditional rule-based programming.
Yes - machine learning systems copy their answers from the internet.

mcqs.q: Does automation remove the need for humans entirely?
options: Yes - machine learning systems copy their answers from the internet.
Yes - an automated factory can run forever with no human input.
No - people are still needed to design, program, monitor and maintain automated systems and to handle unexpected situations.
Yes - automated systems repair and reprogram themselves completely.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Machine learning”?
options: A branch of AI in which systems improve their performance by learning patterns from data rather than following explicitly programmed rules.
The simulation of intelligent behaviour by computers, including reasoning, recognising patterns in data and adapting to new inputs.
The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
A system combining sensors, a microprocessor and actuators that carries out a process with little or no human intervention.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Artificial intelligence”?
options: A branch of AI in which systems improve their performance by learning patterns from data rather than following explicitly programmed rules.
The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
The simulation of intelligent behaviour by computers, including reasoning, recognising patterns in data and adapting to new inputs.
A system combining sensors, a microprocessor and actuators that carries out a process with little or no human intervention.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Actuator”?
options: An output device, such as a motor, valve or heater, that the processor switches on or off to act on the physical world.
The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
A system combining sensors, a microprocessor and actuators that carries out a process with little or no human intervention.
A branch of AI in which systems improve their performance by learning patterns from data rather than following explicitly programmed rules.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Automated system”?
options: An input device that measures a physical property such as temperature, light or motion and sends the data to a processor.
The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
A system combining sensors, a microprocessor and actuators that carries out a process with little or no human intervention.
A branch of AI in which systems improve their performance by learning patterns from data rather than following explicitly programmed rules.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sensor”?
options: The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
An input device that measures a physical property such as temperature, light or motion and sends the data to a processor.
The simulation of intelligent behaviour by computers, including reasoning, recognising patterns in data and adapting to new inputs.
An output device, such as a motor, valve or heater, that the processor switches on or off to act on the physical world.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Robotics”?
options: The design and operation of programmable machines that can carry out physical tasks, often repetitive, precise or dangerous ones.
An output device, such as a motor, valve or heater, that the processor switches on or off to act on the physical world.
An input device that measures a physical property such as temperature, light or motion and sends the data to a processor.
A system combining sensors, a microprocessor and actuators that carries out a process with little or no human intervention.

options: 1800 joints
30 joints
60 joints
120 joints
